title: Being followed on the way home with his trumpet and cane
summary: A man followed him home from a job, and a drunk cousin of his wife's passing by saved him from a possible robbery that would have taken his horn.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: That's right, and there's nothing I can do. I mean I say here's - I a guy can't run, they could get at me --

And then -- well, I ran into trouble a couple of times coming home from work, you know, carrying my trumpet in one hand, and my walking cane in the other. So I felt this guy in back of me. I knew I was being followed. And I'd stop to take a look. He was stopped, standing behind a post. I see, yes. I've got company!

I said now, if I got real nervous -- I was shaky, real shaky. I said if I could get -- I've got my subway fare. If I could get down under my window, here in the Bronx, if I can get up to my wife, get somebody, I will. So I was -- I kept stopping, looking back, stopping, looking back, so the last time I stopped I looked down the street and I saw one of my wife's cousins.

And he was double trouble any time, drunk or sober, and was pretty well drunk. So he said Hello, Hermie, how're you doing? Well, we were setting there talking a while. He say, You all right? I say yeah. You all right? I say -- you sure you all right? This guy was coming toward, he could
evidently see -- why I was watching him, or something. The guy passed. He say You sure you're all right? I said oh, yeah, everything's fine.
Because I didn't -- I didn't want him to --
I didn't want him to get into trouble, you know? [PAUSE]
That's one of my wife's good girl friends.
What were we talking -- oh, we were talking about getting around the street.

Yeah, and I didn't -- I wouldn't tell him, this man that was bothering me, he was trying to rob me or something, because I know -- I could imagine what would have happened, you know, because he -- he told me before, he had done -- had done 15 years for some guy, you know. Some guy had handled him wrong, so they had a fight.

Anyway, I finally got upstairs, but it really hurt me. I was so mad! Because I said if a guy sees me, I'm a cripple. I've got a walking stick. Now here's what he's going to do, grab my horn. If he grabs my horn and run I can't catch him. I can't -- if I sit my horn down to fight him, he can pick it up and run. You know, they hit him with the cane, you can pick it up and run. I say that's the worst. It really hurt me. I was really hurt. I'm -- you know. Well.
